content:
Phase 48: plugin distribution — plan submission (round 1).

Plan: docs/phases/plugin-distribution.md (288 lines, 15 sections; branch phase-48-plugin-distribution @ committed). Problem: `tagteam setup` vendors the handoff contract into every project and the copies have forked — 58 on the arbiter's machine, 6 live projects on a 155-line contract with no gatekeeper / one-run rule / AMEND / interjections / GATE_BOUNCE / panel. Proposal: ship the Claude-facing contract as an installable plugin (skill as single source of truth, SessionStart hook, agents), keep the engine in the package, and turn `setup` from vendoring into removing the vendored copy once the plugin is present. Seam rule: if Claude reads it → plugin; if the CLI reads it or a human edits it after seeding → package. Version coupling handled by release.py bumping plugin.json in lockstep + a runtime `tagteam --version` skew warning.

Two rulings requested (section "For the reviewer to rule on"):
1. v1 scope — A (skill only) / B (skill + SessionStart hook) / C (+ agents). Lead recommends B. Falsifiable test attached: B carries no more migration risk than A iff the hook is shown inert without handoff-state.json. Please also weigh the three listed concerns (hook misfire in a tagteam.yaml-but-no-state project or a non-tagteam project; whether agents complicate the remove path; whether "provable in one cycle" is the right bar for something that can break 46 repos at once).
2. Migration set (section "Migration set") — three migrate (bugalizer, northstar/ns-wip-tests, harmonic), three skip (archived/arcprize, archive/qrcode, archive/handoff-test), with handoff-test getting a version note instead of a migration. Ratify or amend; challenge the handoff-test note if that fixture is load-bearing.

Also in the doc: "Decided by the arbiter" (settled, not up for review), "Deliberately not done", "Deferred", "Done means" (success criteria) and "Verification plan". Scope explicitly excludes any change to the contract's text — this phase moves it, it does not edit it.

Note: this is the first cycle after Phase 47 (3.9.0) — a headless reviewer turn now receives tagteam's CLAUDE.md as PROJECT CONTEXT.

Direction approved, but the plan needs one revision before implementation.

Rulings:
- Choose B for v1: skill + SessionStart hook. Defer both agents. The hook is acceptable only with a test proving it exits silently and successfully when `handoff-state.json` is absent or malformed, including in a non-tagteam project.
- Ratify the proposed migration set: migrate `bugalizer`, `northstar/ns-wip-tests`, and `harmonic`; skip the archived/snapshot directories. Keep `archive/handoff-test` pinned and add the proposed historical-version note, subject to confirming no byte-exact fixture assertion consumes that file.

Required plan fixes:
1. Resolve the headless contract source. `tagteam/headless.py` currently sets `SKILL_RELPATH` to the project-local `.claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md`, fails validation when it is absent, and reads that file into every headless prompt. Therefore removing the vendored skill breaks criterion 4 and contradicts the claim that CLI behavior is out of scope. Specify one canonical packaged/plugin-tree source and the exact resolution/fallback order for headless turns, update the affected CLI/tests in scope, and revise the seam statement accordingly. Do not rely on Claude plugin discovery for a prompt composed by tagteam itself.
2. Define safe plugin detection. Presence in a cache directory is insufficient: the installed registry records scope/projectPath while `enabledPlugins` can disable an installed plugin. The plan must say which scopes apply to the target project, require installed-and-enabled state, and fail closed (retain/vendor the skill) on missing or malformed metadata.
3. Define ownership-safe deletion. Criterion 3 cannot be implemented from pathname alone. Require provenance (for example, exact content matching against known tagteam-vendored contract hashes, plus conservative handling of extra files) so `setup` never removes a customized/project-owned handoff skill. Add tests for modified `SKILL.md` and extra files in the directory.
4. Reconcile scope contradictions. Option B means remove `agents/` from Layout, Moves, Scope, roadmap deliverables, and success criteria for this phase. Also, a version-skew check necessarily changes either the contract text, hook, or CLI behavior, while the current plan says all contract text and CLI behavior are out of scope. Name the component that emits the warning and include its changes/tests explicitly.

The one-cycle proof on aegis is a good canary, but record the exact smoke phase/cycle used and verify both interactive skill discovery and tagteam-composed headless prompt loading; they exercise different resolution paths.

Phase 48 plan — round 2 (commit 8a89b5c on phase-48-plugin-distribution). Rulings taken as given: scope B, migration set ratified. All four required fixes addressed; every changed passage is tagged "(r2)" in docs/phases/plugin-distribution.md (288 → 510 lines; four new sections).

1. Headless contract source — new section "The headless contract source". Canonical source for tagteam-composed prompts is the packaged copy tagteam/data/.claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md (importlib.resources); Claude's plugin cache is never read. Resolution order: explicit skill_path → project-local .claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md if present → packaged. validate() errors only when none resolves. Prompt header becomes `=== HANDOFF CONTRACT (project|packaged) ===` — the only prompt change, outside the contract text. Plugin copy and packaged copy pinned byte-identical by a test and by release.py refusing to bump on mismatch (symlink rejected: package data doesn't carry symlinks reliably). Seam statement revised: "if ONLY Claude reads it → plugin"; the contract is read by both, so it exists in both. The round-1 claim that CLI behavior was out of scope is withdrawn explicitly in Scope.

2. Plugin detection — new section "Plugin detection". setup.plugin_status() reads Claude Code's own records under $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude: installed_plugins.json must parse with version == 2; key tagteam@tagteam; a record applies iff scope == user, or scope == project with realpath(projectPath) == realpath(project root); enabledPlugins consulted in user settings.json + project .claude/settings.json + settings.local.json, explicit false anywhere → disabled; installPath must exist and contain skills/handoff/SKILL.md. Everything else → not installed with a reason line → setup vendors as today. `--no-plugin` forces vendoring; there is no flag that forces removal. (Facts checked on the arbiter's machine: v2 schema with scope/projectPath/installPath; swift-lsp is installed but enabledPlugins: false — exactly the case you raised.)

3. Ownership-safe removal — new section "Ownership-safe removal". Provenance by content: scripts/contract_hashes.py walks git history of the packaged SKILL.md (26 distinct blobs as of 3.9.0) into a shipped vendored_contract_hashes.json; release.py regenerates it. Remove only when the directory holds exactly one entry, SKILL.md, whose sha256 is known. Otherwise keep untouched, print why (modified / extra files: …), and do NOT vendor over it — the project's local copy then wins under resolution rule 2. Tests listed: known → removed; modified → kept; known + extra file → kept; empty dir; not installed → vendored; --no-plugin. Stated explicitly and left out of scope: the pre-existing vendoring path (plugin absent) still rmtree+copytree's — the migration depends on it.

4. Scope reconciled — agents removed from Moves, Layout, Scope, roadmap deliverables and success criteria (kept only in the historical "for the reviewer to rule on" record and the Deferred line). Skew warning: the emitting component is the CLI — new subcommand `tagteam hook session-start [--plugin-root DIR]`; hooks.json is a one-liner `command -v tagteam && tagteam hook session-start --plugin-root "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT" || true`. Silent exit 0 when no tagteam.yaml, no handoff-state.json, malformed state, no/bad plugin.json, tagteam not on PATH; otherwise one banner line plus a warning naming plugin minVersion vs installed __version__. Test matrix in the section (subprocess), plus a test pinning hooks.json's command string to the subcommand. This turns the round-1 falsifier into a test. Contract text remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

Also: migration step 2 now names both resolution paths to verify on aegis (interactive discovery with the vendored dir removed; headless turn whose header says `(packaged)`) and requires the impl submission to record the exact aegis phase/cycle. handoff-test: confirmed `grep -rn handoff-test tests/` is empty in this repo; the impl will grep the fixture dir itself before adding the version note. "Done means" is now 8 criteria (3, 4, 6 rewritten; 7 added for headless resolution).

Design calls I made that you may want to push on: packaged copy (not plugin cache) as the headless source; project-local copy winning over packaged when present; hook logic living in a CLI subcommand rather than shell; content-hash provenance from git history rather than a manifest written at vendor time.

The round-1 issues are resolved, and the Option B / migration rulings stand. One implementation-blocking caller contract remains.

`needs_setup()` currently defines setup completeness by the existence of `.claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md`. A successfully migrated plugin-backed project intentionally lacks that file. This is not merely repeated work: `tagteam/worktree.py::_seed_project()` calls `needs_setup()`, runs `setup_main()`, then calls `needs_setup()` again and rolls the newly created worktree back if it is still true. With an applicable user-scoped plugin, `setup_main()` will remove/omit the local skill, the post-check will remain true, and every worktree creation will fail. `session start --launch` also uses this predicate and would rerun setup on every launch.

Required plan amendment: include plugin-aware setup-completeness semantics and audit all `needs_setup()` callers. Specify that the skill requirement is satisfied by either (a) a project-local handoff skill or (b) `plugin_status(project_root).installed`, while templates/checklists remain required. Preserve fail-closed behavior: uncertain plugin status still requires the local skill. Add tests covering `needs_setup()` for installed/enabled, disabled/malformed, and project-scope matching/nonmatching plugins, plus a worktree `_seed_project` regression showing a user-scoped plugin does not trigger the post-setup rollback. Include `tagteam/session.py`, `tagteam/worktree.py`, and their affected tests in scope if behavior or fixtures must change.

Also correct the non-blocking prose claim that installing the plugin without the package yields a clear version message: the approved hook command is deliberately silent when `tagteam` is absent, which is the safer behavior.

Phase 48 plan — round 3 (commit dc80017). One blocking item + one prose correction, both addressed; passages tagged "(r3)".

needs_setup() — new section "Setup completeness". Caller audit confirmed all three sites and your failure modes: setup.run_setup guard (reruns every time), session.py:659 --launch (reruns every launch), worktree.py:318/326 _seed_project (user-scoped plugin → setup omits the skill → post-check still true → every worktree creation rolls back). Semantics: needs_setup is False iff templates AND checklists present AND (local .claude/skills/handoff/SKILL.md OR plugin_status(dir).installed). Fail-closed by construction — (b) is the same predicate the remove path uses, so disabled/malformed/uncertain/other-path plugins still require the local skill, and setup and needs_setup can never disagree about what belongs on disk. Optional `plugin=` parameter so run_setup passes its already-computed status; other callers compute it (two small JSON reads + one stat). Worktree case spelled out: user scope applies to any path → no vendor, no rollback; project scope's projectPath is the main checkout ≠ worktree realpath → not applicable → setup vendors into the worktree as today → no rollback. session.py/worktree.py added to scope only if a signature/fixture forces it. Tests specified: needs_setup matrix (installed+enabled user → False; disabled → True; malformed → True; project scope matching → False; non-matching → True; plugin installed but templates/checklists missing → True); test_worktree regression for both scopes; test_session --launch no-rerun. Plugin state injected via CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointing at real fixture JSON, not monkeypatched internals. "Done means" criterion 8 added.

Prose: the "clear message when the plugin is installed without the package" claim is withdrawn — the hook is deliberately silent without tagteam on PATH; skew warning covers package-too-old only; plugin-without-package surfaces at the first `tagteam` command the contract prescribes, as today.

Approved. Option B (skill + inert SessionStart hook) and the ratified migration set are now backed by explicit headless resolution, fail-closed plugin detection, ownership-safe removal, version-skew behavior, and plugin-aware needs_setup/session/worktree semantics with regression coverage. Plan commit dc80017.
